title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Q-Planning: Self-Improving Robot Policies

### The Breakthrough
The authors introduce Q-Planning, a framework that pairs a frozen large visuomotor behavior‑cloning policy with a lightweight off‑policy Q‑network. At inference the system samples multiple BC actions, computes a Q‑weighted average, and fine‑tunes only the Q‑network on deployment rollouts, yielding gains across benchmarks: LIBERO‑110 (93 %→99 %), RoboTwin (83.8 %→91.4 %), and real‑world bimanual tasks (stack‑cups 40 %→90 %, insert‑wallet 25 %→80 %). This demonstrates a practical path to continual learning for high‑capacity robot policies.

### The Caveats
The self‑improvement claim is unproven beyond the two bimanual tasks; no single‑arm or other morphologies were evaluated.

## VT-MUSE: Unified Visuotactile Representation

### The Breakthrough
VT-MUSE learns unified sequential representations from visual and tactile streams via a two‑stage pipeline: cross‑modal temporal alignment with masked‑view consistency, then a conditional variational latent model feeding a lightweight Transformer policy through gated cross‑attention. The approach outperforms the strongest baseline by 11 percentage points on a simulation benchmark and improves performance in real‑world trials.

### The Caveats
No baselines are named, so the reported 11‑point improvement cannot be assessed against known prior methods.

## ViTacPhys: Physical Property‑Aware Grasping

### The Breakthrough
ViTacPhys combines temporal visual‑tactile modeling with cross‑attention fusion and a vision‑language semantic prior to predict object mass, friction class, and stiffness. Trained on 60 objects it achieves 97.2 % mass and 98.8 % friction classification (seen objects) and 5.51 % stiffness MAPE, and transfers these estimates to an online adaptive grasping policy that improves real‑world success and force consistency.

### The Caveats
Results are shown only on a single robot with a 60‑object dataset, leaving generalization to other platforms or larger collections uncertain.

## NeSAM: Neuro‑Symbolic Off‑Road Mobility

### The Breakthrough
NeSAM fuses an analytical Bekker‑Wong terramechanics model with a learned residual Transformer dynamics model and adapts soil parameters online via an EKF. This hybrid design cuts prediction error by up to 30 % in simulation and 29 % on real data, and reduces Hausdorff distance to the reference trajectory by 69.4 % in closed‑loop control.

### The Caveats
The paper never names or compares against existing off‑road kinodynamic or terrain‑adaptation baselines, so the magnitude of improvement is unclear.

## Humanoid Sprint & Jump Records

### The Breakthrough
The X‑Humanoid platform demonstrated a 100 m sprint in 9.39 s (beating Usain Bolt’s 9.58 s) and a standing high‑jump of 2.88 m, showcasing high‑speed locomotion and powerful leg actuation in a bipedal robot.

### The Caveats
These one‑off exhibition results lack independent verification or systematic testing, making the claimed superiority over human records unsubstantiated.

## cosmo-edge: Multi‑Platform Edge AI Engine

### The Breakthrough
Cosmo‑Edge provides a single C++17 codebase that abstracts BMRT, RKNN, and other NPU runtimes, delivering a consistent video‑ingest, orchestration, and observability pipeline with built‑in VLM support at 0.1 FPS per channel for up to six streams, plus a multi‑platform benchmark suite and an agent‑assisted model‑porting workflow.

### The Caveats
The reported 0.1 FPS VLM throughput is presented without comparison to existing edge AI frameworks, so performance relative to the state of the art is unclear.

## Varkos: Real‑Time AI Companion for Skyrim

### The Breakthrough
Varkos streams audio through a custom‑optimized Qwen3‑ASR 1.7B model achieving 40‑180 ms latency, combines continuous voice activity detection with a persistent planning layer that tracks world events, and runs local LLM inference for instant action selection, enabling a low‑latency, multi‑step AI partner in Skyrim.

### The Caveats
The demo consists only of an informal video; no measured latency, success rates, or baseline comparisons are provided, leaving the low‑latency claim unverified.

### Priority
Q‑Planning offers a concrete, reproducible method for robots to keep learning after deployment, bridging imitation and reinforcement learning with clear performance gains on both simulation and real‑world tasks.

### One action
Integrate a lightweight off‑policy Q‑network with your existing frozen BC policy and evaluate self‑improvement on a simple manipulation benchmark.

### What to watch
The manipulation papers (Q‑Planning, VT‑MUSE, ViTacPhys) explore complementary paths to smarter robots: Q‑Planning focuses on policy self‑improvement via value‑weighted action selection, VT‑MUSE unifies visual and tactile streams for richer state encoding, and ViTacPhys injects explicit physical property estimates into grasping. Watching how these ideas converge—e.g., adding Q‑weighted updates to multimodal latent spaces or conditioning value functions on material properties—could yield the next leap in adaptable manipulation.
